August 9, 2026

Trump-linked oil firm plans Greenland drilling without government approval

tags: politics, energy, climate
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

A Texas-based company called Greenland Energy is preparing to spend about $60 million drilling two exploratory wells in remote parts of Greenland, according to The Guardian. The company, described as linked to Donald Trump, has not received permission from Greenland's government, which has issued a strong warning ahead of the operation. Drilling has not yet begun. Critics characterise the plan as an attempt to take Greenland's natural resources without a military deployment.

Israel said to be preparing unilateral strikes on Iran

tags: war, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @aaronparnas

Israeli News Channel 13 reported that Israel has concluded the United States is not willing to go far enough to achieve Israel's objectives against Iran. Israel is therefore preparing to resume strikes on Iran unilaterally and to the extent it sees fit. Iran has separately said it is not reopening its strait or reversing its moves anytime soon.

Pentagon gives contractors 21 days to boost weapons output as Iran war drains stockpiles

tags: defence, war, markets
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Pentagon has given defense contractors 21 days to identify ways to rapidly increase weapons production as the war with Iran depletes US stockpiles. The US has reportedly expended more than 850 Tomahawks, roughly 1,000 Patriot and THAAD interceptors and 1,300 tactical ballistic missiles. Industry is being asked to accelerate deliveries, expand production and add new manufacturing capacity.

Attorney General Todd Blanche appears in the Epstein files he oversaw redacting

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Documents in the Epstein files include Todd Blanche, now Attorney General and previously Donald Trump's personal criminal defense attorney. Emails show Blanche discussing Epstein's criminal case around the time of Epstein's 2019 arrest, when Blanche was in private practice at the law firm Cadwalader. The names of those he corresponded with are redacted, and the redactions do not involve victim or survivor information. Blanche oversaw those redactions while serving as deputy attorney general.

Massie says starting a Middle East war is the administration's costliest blunder

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Representative Thomas Massie wrote that of the administration's actions — including withholding Epstein files, attempting tariffs without Congress, advocating more spending, ignoring DOGE and indemnifying glyphosate — starting a war in the Middle East will prove the biggest and most costly. The post came as US munitions stockpiles are being drawn down by the conflict with Iran.

Flock camera error leads police to hold innocent Wisconsin driver at gunpoint

tags: surveillance, policing
sources: @aaronparnas, @ericmoutsos

Brookfield police stopped a car on I-94 in Waukesha County, Wisconsin, with weapons drawn after a Flock automated license plate reader flagged the vehicle as connected to an active Milwaukee homicide investigation. Police say it was both the wrong car and the wrong people; when Brookfield contacted Milwaukee, Milwaukee said it no longer needed the vehicle or occupants and the driver was released. Milwaukee Police Chief Jeffrey Norman has defended the Flock system as a tool to remove violent offenders from the street. The Dane County board had voted to pull funding for Flock contracts over trust concerns before later restoring it.

Democrats prepare wide-ranging investigations of Trump and linked companies

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Democrats in Congress are preparing extensive investigations targeting Donald Trump, his family, his businesses and companies tied to his administration, including BlackRock, Palantir and Tesla. Control of either the House or the Senate in January would give them the gavel and subpoena power. Targets named include the Trump Revocable Trust, which holds his business and real estate assets, along with donors to the ballroom project and other initiatives.

New Orleans to route 911 calls through AI answering agents

tags: tech, policing
sources: @aaronparnas

The Orleans Parish Communications District, the emergency dispatch agency for New Orleans, is integrating AI answering agents into its workflow, according to the Shreveport Times. The tool, described as AI emergency call triage, is meant to prioritise calls, escalate higher-priority emergencies to human dispatchers and automatically handle repeat calls about ongoing incidents. Experts have raised concerns about callers who cannot verbally communicate their situation, such as someone being abducted.

Man publicly plans to release 1,000 pigs in Dearborn's Muslim community

tags: legal, policing
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Videos posted by a man identifying himself as Steve in Alabama describe a plan to transport around 1,000 pigs to Dearborn, Michigan, and stage an accident releasing them, targeting the city's large Muslim population. A follow-up video says the group is concealing its location after being stopped twice while collecting additional loads. Michigan's ethnic intimidation law, MCL 750.147b, enhances penalties for crimes motivated by religion or national origin, and such an act could also implicate federal hate crime and religious freedom statutes as well as conspiracy charges.

Cassidy backs Blanche confirmation while acknowledging criticism

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Senator Bill Cassidy said he would vote for Todd Blanche's confirmation, stating that he expected to be criticised for the vote. The vote is being scrutinised alongside Blanche's confirmation as Attorney General.

Trump posts through the night on Truth Social amid Iran standoff

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

Donald Trump posted extensively on Truth Social over a 24-hour period, including a rendering of a proposed drone port on the White House roof above his planned ballroom featuring service members, drones and vehicles. He also attacked Abdul El-Sayed, the Michigan Democratic Senate nominee, and his wife, and touted 40 club championships won at his own clubs. The posting came as Iran said it would not reverse its recent moves anytime soon.

New Lincoln Memorial signs blame prior administrations for drained reflecting pool

tags: politics, surveillance
sources: @aaronparnas

Signage installed at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool states the pool has been partially refilled so contractors can flush the piping system for the first time in more than a decade. The text attributes the condition to years of neglect by prior administrations, saying more than half of the 58 water supply ports were so clogged they were deemed non-functioning. The pool is currently half filled, and cameras have been installed across the National Mall to deter people from entering it.
